name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
summary_text: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines demands real caution — the Eastern Caribbean outlier: its High Court UPHELD the buggery laws in 2024 (unlike its neighbours), so criminalisation (10 years) remains formally in force. Enforcement is rare, but the legal floor and judicial hostility distinguish it from the decriminalised neighbours.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents Eastern Caribbean constitutional challenges; Saint Vincent and the Grenadines retains colonial-era buggery and gross-indecency laws.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: High Court Decriminalizes Gay Sex | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This HRW article is about Antigua and Barbuda's 2022 ruling, not Saint Vincent and the Grenadines specifically; included as Eastern Caribbean regional context.

sources.title: Gay Life in St Vincent and The Grenadines - GlobalGayz
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Life in St Vincent and The Grenadines' (Sept 2012): 'A Bad Situation and a Bad Law' - homosexuality is illegal, stigmatised and not tolerated; St Vincent has no LGBT organisation (unlike Grenada); most LGBT people marry opposite-gender spouses or live on the 'down-low'; the Caribbean HIV/AIDS Alliance bridges the gap indirectly.

sources.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines court to uphold ban on gay sex
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Feb 2024): Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' High Court upheld the ban on gay sex - sections 146 (up to 10 years for anal intercourse) and 148 (5 years for 'gross indecency') of the Criminal Code 1988 remain; the challenge by Kevin Vinc Johnson and Sean Macleish, who said they were forced to leave the country, was rejected; Justice Esco Henry found the laws 'reasonably required'.

sources.title: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: LGBT People Face Bias | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (July 2023): 'Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: LGBT People Face Bias' - documents discrimination and violence against LGBT Vincentians ahead of the court ruling.

sources.title: High Court ruling undermines the rights of LGBTQ+ Vincentians – ECADE
sources.claim_summary: ECADE press release (Feb 2024): 'High Court ruling undermines the rights of LGBTQ+ Vincentians' - the dismissal of the challenge to sections 146 and 148 'weaponised hate... sanctioned by the highest court' (VincyCHAP); the Attorney General was joined by religious groups as interested parties; the ruling legitimises violence and abuses.
